sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between Seraphim, Chayos, and Ofanim, linking the concept of "ra'ash" (commotion) to the letters forming "se'ar" (hair) and "sha'ar" (gate), and how contemplation of extreme Divine contraction leads to a wide gate for all elevations.

translations.translation: And this will be understood with a prior explanation of the difference between Seraphim, Chayos, and Ofanim,
for, behold,
the Seraphim stand above Him,
and say "Kadosh" etc.,
because their station is in the World of Beriah,
for Imma Ila'ah
(Binah)
nests in Korseya,
and therefore they comprehend how Ein Sof is holy and separate etc.,
and therefore there is no matter of commotion for them,
because it comes within their comprehension etc.
But not so the holy Chayos, whose station is in the World of Yetzirah,
where the aspect of Binah itself does not shine
(as in the World of Beriah),
but rather through its enclothing in the six Sefiros that nest in Yetzirah,
they do not comprehend etc.,
and due to the lack of comprehension because of the concealment and hiding in the World of Yetzirah relative to the World of Beriah,
the matter of commotion occurs for them.
And especially the Ofanim, who are lower,
as it is written,
"one ofan upon the earth,"
and its Targum is "from below,"
and it is explained in Likkutei Torah
(in the weekly portion)
that this is the root and source from which, through the multiplicity of descent, an aspect of evil will be generated,
behold, for them the commotion is even greater.
And, behold,
"ra'ash" (commotion) are the letters of "se'ar" (hair)
(with a left shin),
and the letters of "sha'ar" (gate)
(with a right shin).
"Se'ar"
(with a left [shin])
is the matter of hairs,
which indicates the diminution of vitality through the multiplicity of tzimtzumim,
to such an extent,
that even when one cuts the hairs, he does not feel pain.
For, behold,
it is known
that the opposite of pleasure is felt more intensely than the matter of pleasure,
and therefore,
from the fact that one does not feel pain when cutting the hairs, the greatness of the contraction of vitality in the hairs is most proven.
And "sha'ar"
(with a right [shin])
is as it is written,
"This is the gate to the L-rd,"
like the analogy of a wide gate
(not just a narrow path)
used for entrance and exit.
And this is the matter of "ra'ash" being the letters of "se'ar" and the letters of "sha'ar" in the service of man,
that when a person contemplates that the entirety of the Divine light enclothed in the worlds is an extremely contracted light
(like the analogy of hairs),
and within the aspect of the light enclothed in the worlds itself there are many tzimtzumim until the aspect of "one ofan upon the earth,"
which is the root of the existence of evil
(as above),
and until the multiplicity of tzimtzumim that draw vitality down to the lowest,
lower even than the revelation in the aspect of the Ofanim,
behold, through this contemplation a great commotion is generated
(even more than the commotion in the aspect of the Ofanim),
and through this a wide gate is made for all elevations and draw-downs.
And this is also the matter of the Torah that descended below and became enclothed in human intellect,
that this matter is accomplished through the multiplicity of tzimtzumim,
which is the matter of hairs
("se'ar" with a left [shin]),
and about this it is said,
"His locks are curled,"
"mounds upon mounds of halachos,"
which refers to the halachos of the Torah, about which it is written,
"Salselah (clarify it) and it will exalt you,"
that through clarifying and sifting the hairs to separate the halachos so that there is no difficulty from one to another,
through this the soul is elevated,
and this means,
that specifically through the study of the halachos of the Torah as they descended and became enclothed in physicality through the multiplicity of tzimtzumim, which is the matter of hairs
("se'ar" with a left [shin]),
a gate is made
(with a right [shin])
wide for all elevations and draw-downs etc.
However,
the main matter of the wide gate is accomplished through the service of teshuvah.
For, behold,
the service of fulfilling the Torah and mitzvos that are enclothed in physical things,
behold it is in a manner that the physical things are only a root for the existence of evil
(as above in the explanation of "one ofan upon the earth,"
whose Targum is "from below,"
which is only a root of the existence of evil),
but not so the service of teshuvah, which is after one has sinned and blemished and transgressed the path etc.,
which is an existence of actual evil that fell in the breaking of the vessels etc.,
behold, since the tzimtzum
(the matter of hairs,
"se'ar" with a left [shin])
is greater,
behold also the commotion generated through this is greater,
and consequently through this a gate
(with a right [shin])
is made that is even wider.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that although the revelation of the Surrounding Light will be in the future, it is brought about specifically through our service now, including teshuvah, so that a foretaste of that future revelation exists already in the present.

translations.translation: And based on this, the meaning of "See now etc." will be understood.
For, behold,
even though the revelation of the Sovev (Surrounding Light), which is the boundless light
(through which the true matter of unity is achieved,
"I am He"),
will be in the future, at the Resurrection of the Dead,
nevertheless,
this revelation is accomplished specifically through the service in the present time,
as our master, the Alter Rebbe, said,
that all the revelations of the days of Mashiach and the Resurrection of the Dead depend on our deeds and service throughout the time of the exile.
Therefore it is said, "See now etc.,"
for,
from the perspective of the service of Torah and mitzvos that are enclothed in physical things,
and especially from the perspective of the service of teshuvah,
there exists even now a foretaste of the revelation of the future.
And with this will also be understood the meaning of "You have affirmed the L-rd today etc., and the L-rd has affirmed you today etc., to guard all His commandments."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "As an eagle stirs up its nest" refers to the arousal of great mercy that follows the service of Elul, which is a bottom-up service of teshuvah, and through this a wide gate is opened to draw down mercy and rectify all blemishes, even for the righteous.

translations.translation: e)
And this is the meaning of "As an eagle stirs up its nest," which is an arousal
of great mercies of the aspect of "nesher" (eagle),
that comes after the preparatory service of the month of Elul, which is a service from below upward,
as the acronym of Elul: "I am
to my Beloved and my Beloved is to me,"
except that there is upon this a granting of power from above,
but the service itself is in a manner of from below upward,
for in general it is the matter of the service of teshuvah, which is a service from below upward.
This is "He guarded him as the pupil of His eye,"
"the pupil of His eye" is the black [part] of the eye, and nevertheless the essential power of sight is specifically through the pupil,
and likewise will it be understood in the service of man,
that specifically through the service of teshuvah in a from-below-upward manner, which is the matter of blackness and concealment,
behold, from the aspect of "se'ar"
(with a left shin)
a wide drawing is made to arouse great mercies from the aspect of the Merciful Father and Father of Mercy,
to draw down and rectify all the blemishes that one blemished in positive commandments and negative commandments.

And this is the continuation of the verses: "He guarded him as the pupil of His eye, as an eagle stirs up its nest, hovers over its young, spreads its wings, takes them, bears them on its pinions; the L-rd alone will lead him,"
that through the service of "the pupil of His eye," which is the service of teshuvah as above,
through this, "as an eagle stirs up its nest" is the matter of drawing down mercies to fill all the blemishes,
both in positive commandments, which is the matter of "He will bear them on His pinions," which refers to the 248 positive commandments, the 248 limbs of the King,
and in negative commandments, which is the matter of "the L-rd alone will lead him"
(also, the L-rd Himself includes positive and negative commandments,
"Vav-Hei" is positive commandments and "Yud-Hei" is negative commandments),
that all these matters are rectified through the drawing down of mercies that come through the service of teshuvah, which is the matter of "the pupil of His eye."
And in truth,
behold, according to what was explained above regarding the matter of the wide gate that is made specifically through the hairs,
behold, through the service of "the pupil of His eye," not only are all the blemishes filled,
but rather through the service of teshuvah, a higher light is drawn down than the light drawn down through the service of Torah and mitzvos,
and therefore even the righteous need the service of teshuvah.
And this is the entire matter of the service of the month of Elul in a from-below-upward manner,
that through this the drawing down of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy is accomplished on Yom Kippur, in forgiveness and atonement for all blemishes,
and not only are the blemishes filled, but a higher light is drawn down,
and this is what at the conclusion of the Neilah prayer they say "Shema Yisrael etc." and conclude with "Next year in Jerusalem,"
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Mashiach,
for Mashiach comes to bring the righteous to teshuvah,
which is the drawing down of the aspect of the wide gate also for the righteous.
